title: The coat (Genesis 37:1–11)
hookLine: a favored son, a many-colored coat, and dreams that anger his brothers
last: TO SEE YOUR FACE IS LIKE SEEING GOD.

cards: In some family group chats, everyone knows who the favorite is. The birthday that gets the bigger post. The news that gets three heart emojis from Dad.
Nobody says it. Everybody sees it. Jacob's family has a favorite too: Joseph, seventeen, Rachel's first son, born when Jacob was old.

Rachel, the wife Jacob loved most, has died. Joseph is out with his brothers and the flocks, and he brings back a bad report about them to their father. Today Joseph's story begins, with a piece of clothing.

teach.h: LOVED MORE THAN ALL HIS CHILDREN.
teach.b: In the King James Bible: "Now Israel loved Joseph more than all his children, because he was the son of his old age: and he made him a coat of many colours."
Many colors is the well-known version, but translators aren't sure what the Hebrew means. Some modern translations say a long robe with sleeves, the kind you wear when you don't do field work.
The same words turn up in Second Samuel, for a robe worn by a king's daughter. Either way, everyone could see it. The coat said, every day, this one is different.
And the brothers: "they hated him, and could not speak peaceably unto him." Then Joseph has dreams.
The brothers' sheaves of grain bow down to his sheaf. The sun, the moon and eleven stars bow down to him. And he tells them, both times.
Even Jacob rebukes him for the second. But the text adds: the brothers envied him, but his father kept the saying in mind. Nobody in this scene is innocent.
A father playing favorites. A teenager who can't keep his dreams to himself. Brothers whose resentment is hardening into something worse.

teach.h: THE SON OF HIS OLD AGE.
teach.b: Genesis doesn't make anyone a villain yet. It shows the cost of favor, paid by everyone in the house. Isaac loved Esau; Rebekah loved Jacob.
Jacob grew up in a house of favorites, and now he builds another one.

how: The Joseph story is often taught to children through the coat, and preachers use Genesis 37 to talk about favoritism and envy in families.

games.q: you're Joseph, seventeen. you've dreamed that your brothers' sheaves bowed down to yours. they already can't speak kindly to you. what do you do?
games.why: he tells them, and then has a second dream and tells that one too. "and they hated him yet the more."

practice: Look at a family, an office, a team or a classroom you're part of: who is the favorite, and who never quite gets the coat? Then the harder part: is there anywhere you're the one handing out coats?
See it without judging yourself harshly, think of one small way to even things out, and if you pray, you can ask for a fair heart.

wordCard.voice: The coat. The special robe Jacob gave Joseph, his favorite son: a sign of love, and a daily reminder to his brothers that they were loved less.

orig.note: Hebrew: the well-known coat. the meaning of passim is uncertain: many colors, or reaching to the hands and feet.

carryVoice: Your line: favor has a cost. The whole house paid it. That's day three hundred sixty-six.
